title: 2020 AMC 12B 23
statement: How many integers \(n \ge 2\) are there such that whenever \(z_1,\) \(z_2,\) \(\ldots,\) \(z_n\) are complex numbers such that \[ |z_1| = |z_2| = \cdots = |z_n| = 1 \] and \[ z_1 + z_2 + \cdots + z_n = 0, \] then the numbers \(z_1,\) \(z_2,\) \(\ldots,\) \(z_n\) are equally spaced on the unit circle in the complex plane?

solutions.text:
For \(n = 2,\) \(z_1 + z_2 = 0\) forces \(z_2 = -z_1,\) which is equally spaced. For \(n = 3,\) three unit vectors summing to zero must form an equilateral triangle, so they are equally spaced.

For every even \(n\ge4,\) choose \(\frac{n}{2}\) antipodal pairs at generic angles that do not form a regular \(n\)-gon. For every odd \(n\ge5,\) choose the vertices of an equilateral triangle together with \(\frac{n-3}{2}\) generic antipodal pairs. Each construction has sum \(0\) but is not equally spaced.

Hence only \(n = 2\) and \(n = 3\) work, giving \(2\) values.

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Check small cases: \(n = 2\) forces antipodal points and \(n = 3\) forces an equilateral triangle
For \(n \ge 4,\) build a counterexample by combining a smaller balanced configuration with an antipodal pair
